evidence: Large-scene geometry benchmarks; 2DGS and CityGaussian settings; up to 10x compression, at least 25% training-time savings and 50% memory reduction.
rationale: Efficiency is supported by reported storage, training and memory reductions; geometric accuracy is evaluated on large-scene geometry benchmarks. Claims remain scoped to reconstruction.

evidence: Batch-mode pool-based active learning; DAGGER policy transfer to similar-domain datasets; comparisons with imitation learners and active-learning heuristics.
rationale: The title describes imitation learning; reported dataset experiments and comparator classes support the stated active-learning improvements within similar domains.

evidence: Multiple simulated and real-life anomaly-detection tasks; combined Good-GAN and Bad-GAN; few available anomaly examples.
rationale: The title's explicit 'may' makes necessity tentative; experiments with the combined model support that possibility without asserting universal necessity.

evidence: Language-model text-completion experiments; target-content incorporation and zero-shot control of high-level text attributes.
rationale: Controlled-generation experiments support CoCon's stated functions, but the broad claim of remarkable capabilities across pretrained Transformer language models exceeds the specified evaluation.

evidence: GPT-4 and NLLB comparisons; Xhosa-English gains of 4 BLEURT, 2.5 COMET, and 3.8 BLEURT; eight directions average 6 COMET gain.
rationale: Named low-resource translation comparisons support gains, but any-language-pair applicability and preserved LLM generality extend beyond eight evaluated translation directions.

evidence: Theory with adequately preset weight polarities; learning simulations; image-classification transfer experiments; explicitly illustrated settings where preset polarities are disadvantageous.
rationale: Unrestricted sufficiency conflicts with acknowledged disadvantages; artificial-network theory and simulations do not establish why biological neuronal polarities remain stable.

evidence: Long-video benchmarks on one pretrained model without fine-tuning; end-to-end latency, KV-cache memory, and accuracy comparisons.
rationale: The title describes sparsification and its training setting; the abstract's model-agnostic deployment claim extends beyond evaluation on the same pretrained model.

evidence: Environmental-variation experiments; sampling curriculum compared with best policies found through exhaustive grid search; reported lower computational cost.
rationale: Exploiting variation describes an activity and aim; optimal-setting observations are explicitly limited to considered tasks and supported by exhaustive-grid comparisons.

evidence: GPT-4 and GPT-4o; natural-prompt attacks on JailbreakBench; comparisons with leaderboard attacks; Smooth-LLM and Synonym Substitution defenses.
rationale: Named models, attacks, and defenses support the safety-generalization investigation; input dimensionality alone is asserted to make jailbreak existence inevitable without a reported proof.

evidence: CIFAR-10 CNN image classification; privacy-loss and accuracy dependence on local-network topology; optimization under privacy, computation, and storage constraints.
rationale: The abstract confines validation to CNN image classification on CIFAR-10; the flexible DNN-training title implies broader architecture and task coverage.

evidence: Controlled pre-training schedules: estimated up to 15.86× data efficiency; larger-model replay tests: web-navigation success +4.5% and Basque question-answering accuracy +2%.
rationale: Controlled training and larger-model downstream tests support improved scheduling; the large data-efficiency estimate is explicitly qualified and scoped.

evidence: Empirical GCN subgraph-pruning comparisons with current state-of-the-art methods; joint hardness-based training; visualization of pruning.
rationale: Learning to prune describes an activity; reported empirical comparisons and visualizations support the cautiously phrased accuracy and redundancy findings.

evidence: 23 real-world datasets combining simple edges and hyperedges across biology, social media, and e-commerce; evaluation framework; empirical comparisons of existing GNNs.
rationale: Combined-edge datasets substantiate increased benchmark flexibility; attributing prior performance drops to disregarded simple edges lacks a reported causal comparison.

evidence: Specified distributions; orthogonal-invariant training with Gaussian initialization: Ω(d²) versus O(1) samples; single-target all-distribution gap; extensions to regression, Adam, and AdaGrad.
rationale: The question presupposes a general sample-efficiency advantage; reported proofs establish it for constructed distributions and specified invariant training algorithms.

evidence: Four VLMs on PAIRS and SocialCounterfactuals multiple-choice tasks; hidden-layer fairness analysis; inference ablation/amplification compared with training strategies.
rationale: Response-bias and residual-effect analyses across four VLMs and two datasets support the title's unfair-answer assertion and the reported mitigation approach.

evidence: DyGLib comparisons across models, datasets, and tasks: average 7.8× speedup; discretization implementations: 175×; dynamic-property prediction and time-driven-training experiments.
rationale: Reported speedups support efficiency, and demonstrated dynamic-property prediction and time-driven training substantiate the claimed research capabilities.

evidence: ScanObjectNN: accuracy +3.3%; ModelNet40 versus CurveNet: training 2× faster, testing 7× faster, higher accuracy; multiple-dataset state-of-the-art comparisons.
rationale: Benchmark gains support the restrained framework title; a field-wide claim that performance has saturated over several years exceeds the reported comparisons.

evidence: Six benchmarks covering object classification, intent classification, and entity typing; +1.7 accuracy versus specialized methods, +5.3 general-purpose; aggregator ablations up to +2.8.
rationale: The descriptive title makes no result claim; six benchmarks across three task types, comparator gains, and aggregator ablations support the framework's performance claims.

evidence: Four benchmark datasets; poisoning 0.1% or more of training data; comparisons with prevailing attacks and several benchmark defenses.
rationale: Low-poisoning evaluations and comparisons against benchmark defenses support readily available, efficient attack triggers; broader stealth implications are not clearly unsupported.

evidence: Classic and adversarial OOD evaluations; CIFAR-10; FPR95 reduction up to 57.99%; comparison with the previous best baseline.
rationale: Reported classic and adversarial evaluations, including a substantial CIFAR-10 improvement, support the value of informative outlier mining.

evidence: Point supervision with RetinaNet, Rotated FCOS, and Oriented R-CNN; 62.26% on DOTA-v1.0 with Oriented R-CNN.
rationale: Point-supervised training is evaluated with three oriented detectors and a named benchmark; the priority claim is explicitly qualified.

evidence: Several transfer-learning scenarios and target datasets; image classification, object detection, and instance segmentation evaluations.
rationale: The exploratory title fits data-selection evaluations spanning three task types; optimal selection is an aim rather than an established result.

evidence: Epic-Kitchen and EGTEA; unseen kitchens in within-dataset and across-dataset settings; adaptation through class-agnostic object detectors.
rationale: Evidence covers unseen kitchens in two benchmarks; the title generalizes adaptation to new environments more broadly.

evidence: Optimal-adversary guarantee for fixed policies; continuous-control evaluations against previous attacks; ATLA and LSTM-based policies under adversarial observations.
rationale: A fixed-policy optimality theorem and empirical attack strength do not establish that the learned DRL adversary attains the optimum implied by the title.

evidence: Mean inference time 0.54 seconds at 1024x1024 resolution; single feed-forward pass; pilot human comparison with state-of-the-art face-completion methods.
rationale: Resolution and measured inference time directly support the title; a pilot human study supports the reported face-completion comparison.
